subject.title: fix: timed-out agent runs no longer retain MCP processes

question: Should plugin harnesses that build OpenClaw MCP tools use the host lane-timeout lease disposer, or must each harness own an equivalent timeout-cleanup contract?
rationale: Fixing the excluded Codex/Copilot path crosses the plugin-harness API and ownership boundary, so maintainers must choose the permanent contract rather than letting transport ownership implicitly determine MCP lifecycle ownership.

options.title: Use a host-owned cleanup seam
options.body: Provide a narrow internal callback to every harness that builds OpenClaw tools, keeping MCP lease cleanup owned by OpenClaw independently of transport execution.

options.title: Require harness-owned cleanup
options.body: Define and test an equivalent lifecycle contract in each plugin harness, including cancellation-resistant lane timeout behavior.

options.title: Limit this PR to native runs
options.body: Narrow the stated fix and track plugin-harness MCP timeout leakage separately before treating the overall problem as resolved.

recommendation.title: Use a host-owned cleanup seam
recommendation.body: Provide a narrow internal callback to every harness that builds OpenClaw tools, keeping MCP lease cleanup owned by OpenClaw independently of transport execution.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the current aggregate-lease and deferred-retirement design that this ownership choice extends.
